newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil clips losses at close as EU stocks dip.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil clips losses at close as EU stocks dip.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures shaved losses at the close but still finished down on Wednesday, the day ahead of the October contract's expiry.
October gas oil finished down $1.50 a tonne at $244.50 and November off $1.75 at $238.25. It expires at 1100 GMT on Thursday.
Dealers attributed the fall to profit-taking after October this week repeatedly failed to breach $250 a tonne.
Gas oil lost ground versus Brent narrowing its crack spread premium for November contracts to $7.43 at the close from well over $8 at the beginning of the week.

Gas oil wasn't helped by U.S. government EIA statistics showing an unexpected 1.3 million barrel build in distillate stocks last week, in line with Tuesday's API report. The U.S. shortfall in stocks versus a year ago shrank by 1.6 million barrels to 17.1 million, the API said.
But dealers said gas oil found some support from newly released Euroilstock data showing a growing year-on-year shortfall in European Union distillate stocks.
EU distillates stocks, excluding Sweden, at the end of September were 33.47 million barrels less than a year ago, compared to a 25.79 million deficit at end-August.
Distillates fell 2.93 million barrels to 283.35 million barrels during September, Euroilstock said.
Prices also got a helping hand from unfounded rumours of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's death. His press office said he was working at a sanatorium outside Moscow.
Brent was steady at a small loss on the day, trading down six cents at $24.52 a barrel.
